name: Conservatism Bias
description: People revise beliefs in the direction of new evidence, but not far enough. They stay too attached to prior assumptions relative to what a Bayesian update would imply.
design_relevance_note: Most relevant in analytics interpretation, forecasting, experimentation, and product bets: teams can acknowledge new evidence yet still underreact to it, clinging to the prior roadmap story or legacy mental model.
prevalence_note: Well known in judgment-and-decision theory and occasionally useful in experimentation or analytics discussions, but far less common in day-to-day design discourse than confirmation bias, framing, or defaults.

findings.description: Across simple probability-inference tasks, participants revised their posterior probability judgments in the direction of new evidence but not nearly as far as Bayes' theorem prescribes, systematically underweighting diagnostic evidence relative to their priors.
findings.source_title: Conservatism in a simple probability inference task.

findings.description: Three experiments using a novel full-distribution-elicitation method (rather than single point estimates) confirmed conservatism (under-weighting new evidence relative to a Bayesian update) is real but shows substantial individual variation, measured simultaneously with base-rate neglect for the first time at the individual level. Found no systematic relationship between an individual's base-rate neglect and their conservatism -- these are separate, dissociable tendencies, not two faces of the same underlying trait. An independent, methodologically-innovative confirmation of conservative belief updating using a genuinely different measurement approach than Phillips & Edwards' original 1966 paradigm.
findings.source_title: Base rate neglect and conservatism in probabilistic reasoning: Insights from eliciting full distributions
